title: How to work with the Crux team
basis: Source-derived facts plus explicitly labeled teaching recommendations; not a change to Crux's runtime contracts.

teaching_model.agent: A role with responsibilities, context, and tool boundaries.
teaching_model.skill: A reusable procedure a role or the main assistant follows; not a separate teammate.
teaching_model.human_job: State the outcome, evidence, constraints, and permissions; make the judgments reserved for the owner.
teaching_model.specialist_policy: Teach delegation by default for the other seven roles. This is teaching guidance, not a claim that direct requests are disabled.
teaching_model.skill_policy: Many skills remain user-facing capabilities. People can ask for an outcome in plain language without selecting every specialist.
teaching_model.small_change_policy: Do not require the commander or a promptbook for every task. Let the assistant choose the smallest applicable workflow.
teaching_model.authorization: Objectives guide choices but do not grant permission for more work. A skill request is not blanket permission to publish or sign off.

brainstormer.purpose: Explore an idea before choosing what to build.
brainstormer.when: You have a problem or idea, but have not chosen an approach.
brainstormer.ask: Help me explore ways to improve our onboarding before we decide what to build.
expect: A captured session for the historian to file
avoid: Asking it to implement code
Assuming its conversation was saved automatically
brainstormer.handoff: The caller asks the historian to file the session, then the architect to record a decision when appropriate.

commander.purpose: Coordinate an approved promptbook through completion.
commander.when: A plan exists and you want the team to execute it with its gates.
commander.ask: Run the approved promptbook to completion. Preserve its constraints and stop at its named escalation points.
expect: Evidence-backed completion or a named stop
avoid: Expecting it to edit files or implement code itself
Treating permission to run a plan as permission to publish
commander.handoff: Delegates decisions, implementation, review, retrieval, and documentation to their owners.
source_sections: Commissioning reviews, and reading what comes back

night-gardener.purpose: Notice opportunities and leave a grounded morning note.
night-gardener.when: You want a strategic night pass after project activity, or have deliberately scheduled one.
night-gardener.ask: Tend the garden and leave a morning note grounded in our objectives.
provide: Owner-configured preferences and any approved schedule
expect: A morning note and linked artifacts when the turn gate permits
A silent skip when only its own artifacts changed
avoid: Using it as the default feature implementer
Expecting automatic publication, external messages, or schedule installation
night-gardener.handoff: May ask the historian, librarian, and wayfinder for bounded help. The owner reviews proposed follow-up work.
source_sections: The turn gate (first act, every night)

architect.purpose: Turn a chosen direction into a decision and an executable plan.
architect.when: The team needs an architectural decision, plan, or decision review.
architect.request_via: Tell the main assistant what you want decided or planned; let the coordinator assign the architect.
expect: Findings against objectives when reviewing decisions
avoid: Asking it to implement production code
Letting the drafting architect accept its own ADR
architect.handoff: The coordinator commissions a fresh architect for acceptance after council review, and a dev-lead for implementation.

dev-lead.purpose: Lead implementation and integrate independent work units.
dev-lead.when: An approved change needs working, tested code.
dev-lead.request_via: Ask the coordinator to implement the approved plan; it assigns the dev-lead.
avoid: Manually dispatching developers around the lead
Letting the lead commission review of its own integration
dev-lead.handoff: Assigns developer units and their independent reviews. Its caller commissions review of the lead's own work.
source_sections: Carrying the assignment across the fan-out

developer.purpose: Implement one bounded unit and its tests.
developer.when: A dev-lead has isolated an implementation unit.
developer.request_via: Let the dev-lead assign the unit rather than treating the developer as the whole project team.
expect: Verified, contradicted, or unobserved evidence items
avoid: Asking it to re-delegate
Treating DONE as proof of every user outcome
Asking it to approve its own work
developer.handoff: Returns to the dev-lead, which arranges review and integration.
source_sections: Before you write the first test

reviewer.purpose: Independently judge the assigned outcome and the change.
reviewer.when: Work by another agent is ready for verification.
reviewer.request_via: Ask the coordinator for independent review of the change, not self-approval by its author.
avoid: Asking it to fix the change while reviewing
Letting the author commission its own review
reviewer.handoff: Reports to the delegator that commissioned the work. The implementer handles fixes.
source_sections: Who commissions you, and what you are given

historian.purpose: Preserve work in the documentation tree through its owning skills.
historian.when: The team needs filing, journal entries, run records, documentation maintenance, or archival.
historian.request_via: Say what should be saved or maintained; let the main assistant dispatch the historian.
provide: The content or result to preserve
What the write must leave unchanged
expect: Paths and limitations in the handoff
avoid: Asking it to implement source code
Bypassing inbox processing to file a brainstormer's session
historian.handoff: Receives content from other roles and files it through the appropriate skill.
source_sections: What you do (always via the owning skill, never raw freehand)
The write you were dispatched to make arrives as an assignment

librarian.purpose: Retrieve recorded project knowledge with citations.
librarian.when: A question can be answered from the project's documentation tree.
librarian.request_via: Ask the main assistant the question, such as why a decision was made; it can dispatch the librarian.
expect: A distilled answer with document paths
An explicit gap when the tree does not answer
avoid: Asking it to invent missing facts
Asking it to make new architectural decisions or write records
librarian.handoff: Returns facts to its caller; requests for judgment belong to the architect and writes to the historian.

wayfinder.purpose: Assess a large or uncertain source before it fills the caller's context.
wayfinder.when: An agent needs to triage a file, corpus, or external source.
wayfinder.request_via: Let the agent doing the work delegate source triage with a specific purpose.
provide: Source paths or explicitly named external sources
expect: A fit, unfit, or partial verdict
A condensed digest with source locations
avoid: Asking it to run commands or change files
Passing local private text into outbound searches
Using it instead of the librarian for ordinary recorded-fact lookup
wayfinder.handoff: Returns a digest to its caller; the caller decides what to read or do next.

skill_notes.run-promptbook: This skill changes run state; the commander orchestrates the whole run. For status questions use visualize-run-progress.
skill_notes.visualize-run-progress: Status questions do not authorize advancement. Optional artifact output is distinct from a read-only status answer.
skill_notes.derive-arch: Regeneration writes generated architecture files. Ask query-docs to explain the current architecture without rebuilding it.
skill_notes.link-adr-graph: Generating a lineage artifact is different from asking what supersedes what; route the question to query-docs.
skill_notes.query-docs: Questions about current architecture or decision relationships are retrieval, not permission to regenerate.
skill_notes.check-drift: Does not regenerate outputs. Check the selected version's workflow for operation-log side effects before describing the whole invocation as write-free.
skill_notes.audit-docs: May repair safe drift; it is not interchangeable with a non-regenerating drift check.
skill_notes.review-decisions: Produces findings and review records, but does not enact the findings.
skill_notes.refresh-research-synthesis: Rewriting synthesis requires explicit per-page approval.
skill_notes.escalate-arch-runtime: Explicit human request and the skill's separate consent conditions are required. Never an automatic remedy for failed static extraction.
skill_notes.propose-observation: The body contract requires human invocation even though the frontmatter does not declare disable-model-invocation.
skill_notes.transition-adr: Acceptance requires the appropriate decision process; a drafting architect cannot accept its own decision.
skill_notes.propose-brief: Scaffold-only by default; the documented whiteboarding-session intake path is a distinct exception.
skill_notes.srde: Dissent resolution is bounded by the workflow's escalation rules; it is not unlimited authority to continue.
skill_notes.tend-garden: The owner establishes any schedule. The role must pass its turn gate and may not push, merge, or send externally.
skill_notes.survey-sheet: A human-invoked scaffold, not a sign-off; leaves verdicts and rationale for the human.
skill_notes.survey-signoff: The human supplies and confirms verdicts. The agent must not invent approval.
skill_notes.reconcile-signoff: The human supplies the verdict and rationale for one pairing; do not batch-sign.
skill_notes.backfill-signoff: Owner sign-off is required. Presentation of this skill is not delegated approval.

audience_definitions.human_request: An outcome a person can request from the main assistant; naming or manually launching a specialist is not required.
audience_definitions.explicit_human: A deliberate human invocation is required by a declared flag or body contract. Use the harness's supported explicit invocation path.
audience_definitions.agent_internal: Team/runtime support; omit from beginner call-to-action lists.
audience_definitions.workflow_support: Normally reached inside a workflow; advanced users may request it where its contract allows.

journeys.user_request: Help me explore this idea before we build it.
journeys.note: This is a conceptual handoff, not a requirement to use every role for every change. The caller coordinates leaf-role handoffs.
The commander commissions review of the lead's own integration; the lead commissions reviews of developer units.
Answer from records; do not turn a question into regeneration.

journeys.user_request: Fix this bounded defect directly; do not change any contracts.
journeys.note: The sizing test still applies. No book or council when the task qualifies.
The turn gate may legitimately produce no output. Suggestions do not authorize publication.

handoff_template.outcome: What improves for the affected user?
handoff_template.objectives: Resolved objectives path plus relevant mission/goals or an instruction to read them.
handoff_template.inputs: Exact source paths, work scope, and prior approved decisions.
handoff_template.report: Separate verified, contradicted, and unobserved claims.

publication_notes: Do not present seven specialist roles as seven more buttons the beginner must learn.
Separate source-declared invocation flags from recommended audiences; enforcement differs across harnesses.
Do not promise that trigger phrases deterministically select a skill.
Declared role skill lists are associations, not a complete call graph or a guarantee a skill can run under every role's tool limits.
Source model aliases are configuration details, not fixed recommendations about vendors or models.
Confirm public release availability before linking a beta-version source or presenting its features as officially released.
